title: VideoGameQA-Bench: Evaluating Vision-Language Models for Video Game Quality Assurance
key_findings: Standard zero-shot VLMs detect coarse bugs (~78% accuracy) but fail severely on micro-clipping and precise bounding boxes, frequently hallucinating on stylized art.
primary_limitations: High inference latency (>1.5s/frame); poor spatial bounding localization for subtle geometry defects.

title: A Hybrid Co-Finetuning Approach for Visual Bug Detection in Video Games
key_findings: Co-finetuning leveraging labelled target frames, co-domain games, and unlabelled gameplay frames with I-JEPA boosts recall by +18.4% mAP without manual exhaustive labels.
primary_limitations: Significant cross-domain degradation when transferring across radically divergent art styles (e.g. realistic 3D to voxel).

title: State-Aware Visual Glitch Detection in Complex 3D Video Games Using Deep Multimodal Representations
key_findings: Fusing game-engine internal telemetry (transform matrices and collision queries) with RGB vision reduces false positives by 41.9% compared to pure vision.
primary_limitations: Requires engine-level instrumentation hooks; cannot be deployed as a black-box tester on closed commercial builds.

title: How Far Can VLMs Go for Visual Bug Detection? Studying 19738 Keyframes from 41 Hours of Gameplay Videos
key_findings: Baseline VLM achieves 0.50 precision and 0.72 accuracy across EA gameplay; Image-RAG degrades precision from 0.50 to 0.37 due to confirmation bias on environmental features.
primary_limitations: Low temporal sensitivity; prompt sensitivity; prone to mistaking intentional stylized art for visual defects.

title: RefGlitch-Bench: A Benchmark for Reference-based Gameplay Glitch Detection with Vision-Language Models
authors: Yu, Wiens, Barahona-Rios, Wilkins, Zadtootaghaj, Barman, Bezemer
key_findings: Formulating glitch detection as an explicit pairwise comparison with the Last Clean Frame dramatically resolves stylistic ambiguity and boosts F1 from 0.42 to 0.69.
primary_limitations: Requires reliable reference frame selection; error propagation occurs when the selected reference frame itself contains subtle artifacts.

title: TempGlitch: Detecting Temporal Visual Glitches in Continuous Gameplay Video Streams
key_findings: Single-frame anomaly detectors miss over 65% of animation and flickering glitches; sliding-window temporal attention over 16-frame buffers is essential for streaming playtests.
primary_limitations: High computational footprint; current video transformer backbones are too heavy for 60 FPS real-time CI playtesting.

title: Weak Supervision for Label Efficient Visual Bug Detection in Video Games
key_findings: Domain-specific weak supervision with just 5 clean exemplar frames improves F1 score from 0.336 to 0.550 in low-prevalence first-person player clipping regimes.
primary_limitations: Evaluated primarily on first-person clipping in a single open-world game; generalisation to other glitch classes unverified.

title: Automatically Detecting Visual Bugs in HTML5 Canvas Games
key_findings: Internal canvas decomposition and oracle sprite comparison achieves 100% accuracy on injected canvas bugs vs 44.6% for naive screenshot diffing.
primary_limitations: Restricted to 2D web canvas games with inspectable DOM/sprite trees; wholly inapplicable to compiled 3D shaders.

title: Video Game Automated Testing Approaches: An Assessment Framework
key_findings: Establishes multi-dimensional quality evaluation taxonomy classifying playability, functional, and graphical glitch automation across commercial game engines.
primary_limitations: Qualitative framework without a standardized empirical test harness.

title: A Literature Review of Software Testing Practices and Frameworks in the Video Gaming Industry
key_findings: Surveys industrial testing pipelines, demonstrating that despite extensive CI/CD adoption, visual verification remains heavily reliant on manual playtesting teams (>80%).
primary_limitations: Survey of human industrial practices rather than an algorithmic vision contribution.

title: A Large-Scale Empirical Study of Video Game Testing Practices
key_findings: Reveals that game developers perceive visual glitch testing as the hardest testing domain to automate, resulting in visual regression tests being skipped in 68% of sprints.
primary_limitations: Empirical interview study without technical algorithmic implementation.

title: Video game testing: a systematic literature review
key_findings: Foundational SLR documenting that traditional software testing methods (unit, integration) fail in video games due to non-deterministic graphics pipelines.
primary_limitations: Pre-dates the deep learning and foundation model revolutions in computer vision.

title: Self-Supervised Contrastive Learning for Object Clipping Detection in Modern 3D Engines
key_findings: Contrastive visual embeddings achieve view-invariant clipping detection without requiring 3D mesh vertex coordinate access during gameplay runtime.
primary_limitations: High false positive rate on complex alpha-blended transparency effects and volumetric smoke.

title: Automating Playtesting for Glitch Detection in 3D Games
key_findings: Demonstrates that curiosity-driven DRL agents can autonomously navigate 3D game levels and uncover boundary clipping bugs 4.2x faster than random exploration.
primary_limitations: Proprietary Frostbite engine implementation; agent policies fail to generalize to new levels without retraining.

title: Deep visual anomaly detection for 3D game environments using multi-view surface projections
model_family: Multi-View Projection CNN + Anomaly Memory Bank
key_findings: Synthesizes multi-angle viewpoints of in-game meshes to build patch-level memory banks, detecting texture tearing and vertex distortions without bug labels.
primary_limitations: Restricted to isolated asset inspection; cannot process dynamic real-time gameplay sequences.

title: Grammar-Based and Constraint-Driven Testing for Collision and Clipping Anomalies in 3D Environments
key_findings: Generates synthetic clipping and collision violations using grammar rules to evaluate automated detector sensitivity systematically.
primary_limitations: Synthetic injection fails to capture organic clipping nuances arising from complex physics interactions.

title: Real-Time Shading and Texture Pop-in Glitch Localization in Continuous 3D Streams
key_findings: Achieves 75 FPS real-time localization of texture pop-in and lighting flickering on 4K game streams using multi-scale temporal differencing.
primary_limitations: Requires GPU compute budget that competes with the game engine during active rendering.

title: Effective Visual Regression Testing for Web and Interactive Applications with Perceptual Image Differencing
key_findings: Incorporating human contrast sensitivity functions (CSF) eliminates 82% of false positive visual regression alarms caused by anti-aliasing jitter.
primary_limitations: Designed for 2D web interfaces; fails under dynamic 3D camera rotation and lighting shifts.

title: ShaderBug: Automated Shader Defect and Rendering Regression Detection via Mutational Fuzzing
key_findings: Uncovers 47 confirmed rendering bugs in GPU drivers and game engine pipelines by fuzzing GLSL/HLSL shaders with differential image comparison.
primary_limitations: Focuses on compiler and shader translation bugs rather than gameplay asset glitches.

title: Action-Conditioned Gameplay Video Anomaly Detection
key_findings: Conditioning video glitch detection on gamepad controller telemetry enables distinguishing intentional character stunts from physics engine ragdoll failures.
primary_limitations: Requires synchronized controller input streams alongside video; unusable on raw spectator video.

title: GlitchHunter: Automated Detection of Character Rigging and Animation Defects in 3D Games
key_findings: Extracts character skeleton bone hierarchies from animation streams, detecting inverse kinematics pops and broken skinning weights with 93.4% accuracy.
primary_limitations: Requires bone transform data or clean character pose estimation; degraded by heavy character clothing occlusion.

title: Wuji: Automatic Online Combat Game Testing via Deep Reinforcement Learning and Evolutionary Algorithms
key_findings: Combines multi-objective evolutionary algorithms with deep RL to explore state spaces in commercial online combat games, finding 41 critical bugs.
primary_limitations: Heavyweight training required per game; relies on hand-crafted fitness functions for defect verification.

title: Autonomous VLM Agents for Exploratory Playtesting and Interactive Bug Localization
key_findings: Embodied VLM agents autonomously navigate game levels and generate natural-language bug reproduction reports, finding 64% of known test issues.
primary_limitations: High API inference latency (2.1s per step); struggles with high-tempo combat scenarios.

title: VLM-UI-Test: Autonomous GUI Testing of Video Games Using Multimodal Foundation Models
key_findings: Parses complex, non-standard mobile game UI screens, detecting button text truncation, icon overlapping, and touch target misalignment across 63 titles.
primary_limitations: Restricted to 2D UI overlay planes; does not verify world-space diegetic UI elements.

title: GlitchBench: Can Large Multimodal Models Detect Video Game Glitches?
key_findings: Evaluates leading MLLMs on 923 game screenshots (593 glitch, 330 clean); GPT-4V achieves only 43.4% accuracy (human baseline: 85.6%), revealing massive domain gap.
primary_limitations: Static single-frame benchmark; does not evaluate temporal animation or rendering frame rate bugs.

title: VideoGameBunny: Towards Vision Assistants for Video Games
key_findings: Instruction-tunes an open-source VLM on 185K images with 389K QA pairs across 413 titles, boosting game QA accuracy by +14.2% over base model.
primary_limitations: Tuned primarily on static image QA; lacks temporal multi-frame sequence reasoning.

title: PhysGame: Uncovering Physical Commonsense Violations in Gameplay Videos
authors: Cao, Tang, Zhao, Guo, Liu, Zhang, Liu, Sun, Reid, Liang
key_findings: Establishes physical commonsense benchmark across mechanics, kinematics, optics, and materials; PhysInstruct (140K QA) significantly improves physical bug detection.
primary_limitations: Evaluates physical plausibility rather than industrial rendering engine shader bugs.

title: CLIP Meets GamePhysics: Towards Bug Identification in Gameplay Videos Using Zero-Shot Transfer Learning
key_findings: Demonstrates that CLIP zero-shot text-image embeddings can retrieve and flag physics glitch videos across 1,873 games without task-specific training.
primary_limitations: Relies on title/description text correlation; poor temporal boundary precision for short glitch events.

title: Large Language Models Are Pretty Good Zero-Shot Video Game Bug Detectors
key_findings: Frames bug detection as QA over textual event logs, achieving 70.66% overall accuracy and up to 78.94% on specific titles without task training.
primary_limitations: Evaluates textual event descriptions rather than raw screen pixels or spatial rendering.

title: LeCuration: A Tiny World Model as a Data Curation Mechanism for Game QA
model_family: Tiny Latent World Model Curation Filter
key_findings: Employs an ultra-compact latent world model (12M params) to filter redundant frames, reducing downstream VLM testing costs by 76% while maintaining bug recall.
primary_limitations: Requires initial video pre-filtering pass; may occasionally discard single-frame visual blips.

title: Using Deep Convolutional Neural Networks to Detect Rendered Glitches in Video Games
key_findings: Pioneering supervised DCNN approach: ShuffleNetV2 on 800x800 frames detects missing, stretched, and low-res textures with 86.8% accuracy, 88% TP rate, and 8.7% FPR.
primary_limitations: Evaluates single static frames on isolated 3D assets; unable to detect dynamic physics or temporal animation bugs.

title: Automated Visual Bug Detection in 3D Video Games Using Deep Convolutional Networks
authors: Davarmanesh, Jiang, Ou, Vysogorets, Ivashkevich, Kiehn, Joshi, Malaya (AMD)
model_family: DFT + HOG + Graph Laplacians Mixed Experts Ensemble
key_findings: Creates open-source Glitchify tool (50K images); ensemble classifier identifies 10 screen artifacts with 84% accuracy on seen games, dropping to 69% on unseen games.
primary_limitations: Domain transfer drop of 15% across unseen game styles; hand-crafted feature extraction overhead.

title: Learning to Identify Perceptual Bugs in 3D Video Games
key_findings: Self-supervised perceptual representation learning captures visual glitch features without task-specific labels, outperforming supervised transfer.
primary_limitations: Limited evaluation environments; high sensitivity to environmental lighting changes.

title: Automated Glitch Detection in Games Using Supervised Neural Classifiers
key_findings: Supervised neural classifiers trained on synthetic glitch augmentations achieve 88.2% F1 on target game test levels.
primary_limitations: Severe over-fitting to specific level art geometry; fails when tested on unseen level environments.

title: Inspector: Pixel-Based Automated Game Testing via Exploration, Detection, and Investigation
model_family: RL Autonomous Exploration + CNN Defect Detector
key_findings: Couples RL navigation agent with vision defect detectors across 10 perceptual bug classes with pixel-level segmentation masks.
primary_limitations: Agent exploration can get stuck in complex geometry; computationally expensive dual-loop system.

title: RiverGame: A Game Testing Tool Using Artificial Intelligence
key_findings: Comprehensive automated testing framework coupling state-transition models with deep visual assertion oracles.
primary_limitations: Requires game state formalization; heavy manual setup overhead per game.

title: GELID: Game Glitch Identification from Video Captions
key_findings: Extracts bug timestamps from long gameplay videos by analyzing streamer audio transcripts and automated speech recognition without processing raw video frames.
primary_limitations: Only works on gameplay footage with expressive human commentary; inapplicable to silent automated CI soak runs.

title: HASTE: Image-Similarity Based Stuttering Bug Event Detection in Gameplay Videos
model_family: Temporal Perceptual Hashing & Optical Flow Differencing
key_findings: HASTE isolates gameplay ROI from streamer overlays and computes inter-frame similarity curves to detect micro-stuttering events with high precision.
primary_limitations: Focuses exclusively on temporal frame rate stability; cannot detect static spatial or texture corruptions.

title: Classifying Gameplay Video Segments as Buggy or Non-Buggy Using Captions
key_findings: Shows that player verbal expressions (exclamations, confusion) paired with video features achieve 83.4% bug detection accuracy across 100+ titles.
primary_limitations: Dependent on vocal streamer presence; cannot be deployed on headless continuous integration test runs.

title: GLIB: Towards Automated Test Oracle for Graphically-Rich Applications
authors: Chen, Li, Chen, Fan, Hu, Yang
key_findings: Automated layout verification discovering 127 visual UI bugs in production graphical applications using visual element hierarchy graphs.
primary_limitations: Designed for 2D UI layouts; inapplicable to dynamic 3D world viewports.

title: Q-Bench: A Benchmark for General-Purpose Foundation Models on Low-Level Vision
authors: Wu, Zhang, Zhang, Chen, Liao, Wang, Li, Sun, Yan, Zhai, Lin
key_findings: Comprehensive proof that high-level semantic VLMs perform poorly at low-level pixel perception (blur, noise, fine-grained rendering artifacts).
primary_limitations: General computer vision benchmark; not specialized to interactive video game engines.

title: A Survey of Video Game Testing
key_findings: Documents that visual regression testing is the least automated sector (<15% automation) across the entire game development lifecycle.
primary_limitations: Taxonomic survey; no empirical CV benchmark.

title: Know Your Bugs: A Survey of Issues in Automated Game Testing Literature
key_findings: Synthesizes academic bug classifications with industrial JIRA schemas, demonstrating severe fragmentation in visual bug definitions.
primary_limitations: Survey without technical CV implementation.

title: Automated Reporting and Verification of Visual GUI Defects in Interactive Applications
key_findings: Automated CV framework verifying visual defect reproduction from screenshots and user reports, achieving 94% precision in GUI element detection.
primary_limitations: Focused on mobile/desktop GUI widgets; not tailored to real-time 3D camera viewports.

title: Towards Automated UI Visual Bug Detection in Cross-Platform Mobile and PC Games
model_family: Deep Object Detection & Aspect Ratio Bounds
key_findings: Identifies that non-standard aspect ratios (ultrawide 21:9, mobile notches) cause 34% of player-reported interface text and HUD clipping bugs.
primary_limitations: Small evaluation scale; evaluated only static screens.
